blueprint_topic: Management of Care — interdisciplinary post-stroke rehabilitation assessment and level-of-care planning
stem: A client recovering from acute ischemic stroke has motor weakness, difficulty with activities of daily living, dysarthria, and cognitive changes. Which action by the RN best supports rehabilitation planning?

options.A: Coordinate interdisciplinary assessment during hospitalization to identify functional needs and help determine the appropriate rehabilitation intensity and setting.
options.B: Base the rehabilitation referral primarily on motor strength because communication and cognitive deficits can be addressed after the level of care is selected.
options.C: Delay rehabilitation-level assessment until discharge instructions are prepared so the client's spontaneous neurologic recovery can be judged first.
options.D: Request separate discipline-specific evaluations without a coordinated plan because each impairment should determine its own post-acute disposition independently.

rationale: A is correct. The 2026 AHA/ASA acute ischemic stroke guideline states that patients have highly variable impairments and individualized needs and that a comprehensive multidisciplinary program is critical for assessing the appropriate intensity and modality of rehabilitation. The guideline also notes that in-hospital interdisciplinary evaluation for the appropriate level of rehabilitation is associated with improved functional outcomes. B is incorrect because rehabilitation planning should address the client's multidimensional functional needs rather than relying mainly on motor weakness. C is incorrect because the guideline supports multidisciplinary inpatient evaluation rather than deferring rehabilitation-level assessment until discharge preparation. D is incorrect because discipline-specific expertise is valuable, but the guideline emphasizes coordinated multidisciplinary assessment to determine an appropriate rehabilitation plan and level of care.
educational_objective: Coordinate multidisciplinary rehabilitation assessment during hospitalization after stroke so motor, self-care, communication, cognitive, and other functional needs inform the appropriate rehabilitation intensity and post-acute level of care.
source_organization: American Heart Association / American Stroke Association
source_document_title: 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke
source_version_date: Originally published January 26, 2026; current free-access guideline rechecked 2026-08-20
source_locator: Section 5.7 Rehabilitation — Synopsis: patients with stroke have highly variable degrees of impairment and diverse individualized needs; a comprehensive multidisciplinary program designed to assess appropriate rehabilitation intensity and modality is critical; in-hospital interdisciplinary evaluation for the appropriate level of rehabilitation is associated with improved functional outcomes. Recommendation-Specific Supportive Text 1: organized inpatient stroke units commonly include interdisciplinary rehabilitation assessment; multiple guidelines support multidisciplinary inpatient evaluation for the appropriate level of rehabilitation after stroke, and early adherence has been associated with improved functional recovery.
source_claim_supported: Post-stroke rehabilitation planning should use coordinated multidisciplinary inpatient assessment because impairments and individualized needs vary and the assessment helps determine appropriate rehabilitation intensity, modality, and level of care.

Removed the 'only' distractor and longest-answer cue and replaced simplistic distractors with realistic errors involving motor-domain overemphasis, delayed assessment, and uncoordinated discipline-specific planning.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly reflects AHA/ASA support for coordinated inpatient multidisciplinary rehabilitation assessment and level-of-care planning.
option_audit.B: Plausible motor-dominant planning error; incorrect because individualized rehabilitation needs extend beyond motor impairment.
option_audit.C: Plausible wait-for-recovery sequencing error; incorrect because rehabilitation-level evaluation is supported during hospitalization.
option_audit.D: Plausible siloed-discipline error; incorrect because the guideline emphasizes a coordinated multidisciplinary program rather than independent disposition decisions.
